Atom.scope: Chemical elements — 118 recognized kinds, corresponding to atomic numbers 1–118; applies to Atom and Elemental substance portion. Element 119 is not an accepted discovery.

ElementalSubstance.scope: Chemical elements — 118 recognized kinds, corresponding to atomic numbers 1–118; applies to Atom and Elemental substance portion. Element 119 is not an accepted discovery.

SubatomicParticle.scope: Elementary particles — 17 Standard Model kinds in the conventional chart: six quark flavours, six leptons, four gauge-boson kinds, and the Higgs boson. Antiparticles and colour states are not counted separately; this is not a count of all composite subatomic particles.

Substance.scope: Chemical substances — over 290 million registered substances in CAS REGISTRY. A catalogue lower bound for known substances, not a count of every possible molecule or compound, nor of physical substance portions.

Mineral.scope: Minerals — 6,239 valid mineral species, IMA-CNMNC master list, 2026.09; kinds represented by Mineral substance portion, not individual mineral grains.

Vitamin.scope: Vitamins — 13 essential vitamin categories for humans, including eight B vitamins; chemical vitamers within a category are not separate vitamins in this convention.

Planet.scope: Planets — eight Solar System planets; 6,445 confirmed exoplanets in the NASA Exoplanet Archive, release 2026.10.08. The exoplanet count is a discovery catalogue, not the estimated cosmic population.

Satellite.scope: Natural satellites — 293 confirmed moons of Saturn, NASA's 2026.08 reference count. This bounded-system count does not imply a total for all natural satellites.

Asteroid.scope: Asteroids — about 1.1–1.9 million main-belt asteroids larger than 1 km, plus millions of smaller bodies; an estimated population, not a discovery-list count.

Comet.scope: Comets — likely billions in the Solar System, NASA's population estimate; a discovery catalogue contains only a small fraction.

Star.scope: Stars — more than 100 billion in the Milky Way, an estimated population within our galaxy.

Galaxy.scope: Galaxies — at least 100 billion in the observable universe, NASA's broad estimate; faint-galaxy extrapolations depend on detection limits and cosmological models.

State.scope: Sovereign states — 195 under the UN convention: 193 member states and two non-member observer states, the Holy See and Palestine. Recognition disputes change broader counts; “nation,” ethnic group, and state are not interchangeable. Applies to State territory and Geopolitical Area.

Continent.scope: Continents — seven in the familiar English-language convention; other conventions use four, five, or six. Applies to Continental area.

SaltWaterArea.scope: Oceans — five named oceans within one connected global ocean; applies to Saltwater area.

StaticWaterArea.scope: Lakes — about 117 million with area at least 0.002 km², the GLOWABO satellite inventory (2014), excluding Greenland and Antarctica. A size-threshold estimate relevant to Standing-water area; lakes are not necessarily freshwater.

Island.scope: Islands — 340,686 mapped marine islands, calculated from 21,818 larger than 1 km² and 318,868 at most 1 km² in the USGS-described 30 m satellite inventory (2014 imagery, 2020 publication). Excludes its five continental mainlands; map resolution and shoreline rules limit completeness.

Human.scope: Humans — about 8.3 billion living individuals in 2026, a rounded global population estimate, not a count of everyone who has ever lived.

Currency.scope: Currency systems and codes — 178 distinct active ISO 4217 alphabetic codes in SIX List One, published 2026.09.17; counted by deduplicating nonempty Ccy fields. Includes funds, precious-metal, testing, and no-currency codes, so this is not 178 circulating national currencies.

Cell.scope: Cells — about 36 trillion in a reference adult male and 28 trillion in a reference adult female, Hatton et al. (2023); model-dependent individual counts, not cell-type counts or a total for all organisms.

HumanLanguage.scope: Human languages — 7,170 living languages, Ethnologue's 29th edition (2026), as reported by Wikipedia. Language-versus-dialect boundaries depend on the catalogue; extinct and constructed languages are outside this total.

NaturalLanguage.scope: Human languages — 7,170 living languages, Ethnologue's 29th edition (2026), as reported by Wikipedia. Language-versus-dialect boundaries depend on the catalogue; extinct and constructed languages are outside this total.

ComputerLanguage.scope: Computer languages — 8,945 programming languages catalogued by HOPL, including historical languages; this roster is not restricted to languages in active use and does not exhaust every possible formal language.

Character.scope: Characters — 172,808 encoded characters in the Unicode 18.0 summary, dated 2026.09.16. The source retains a draft-status notice, so this count is provisional; it counts an encoding repertoire, not every symbol or glyph humans can create.

MeasurementUnit.scope: Measurement units — seven SI base units and 22 derived units with special names, not all possible derived or non-SI units. The SI prefix vocabulary has 24 prefixes.

NaturalNumber.scope: Natural number, Integer, and Rational number — each countably infinite, cardinality ℵ₀.

Integer.scope: Natural number, Integer, and Rational number — each countably infinite, cardinality ℵ₀.

RationalNumber.scope: Natural number, Integer, and Rational number — each countably infinite, cardinality ℵ₀.

Number.scope: Natural number, Integer, and Rational number — each countably infinite, cardinality ℵ₀.
Number.interpretation: Cardinalities of these named number systems, not a total for every numerical extension.

Number.scope: Real number and Complex number — each uncountably infinite, cardinality of the continuum, 2^ℵ₀; a complex number is a pair of real numbers.
Number.interpretation: Continuum cardinality 𝔠 = 2^ℵ₀, uncountably infinite; not asserted to equal ℵ₁.

RealNumber.scope: Real number and Complex number — each uncountably infinite, cardinality of the continuum, 2^ℵ₀; a complex number is a pair of real numbers.

ComplexNumber.scope: Real number and Complex number — each uncountably infinite, cardinality of the continuum, 2^ℵ₀; a complex number is a pair of real numbers.

Algorithm.scope: Algorithm, Computable function, and Recursive function — each countably infinite under the usual finite-description convention. Finite formal expressions, finite symbol strings, and finite graphs of arbitrary size are also countable; this follows by finite-string encoding, not from a survey of existing examples.

ComputableFunction.scope: Algorithm, Computable function, and Recursive function — each countably infinite under the usual finite-description convention. Finite formal expressions, finite symbol strings, and finite graphs of arbitrary size are also countable; this follows by finite-string encoding, not from a survey of existing examples.

RecursiveFunction.scope: Algorithm, Computable function, and Recursive function — each countably infinite under the usual finite-description convention. Finite formal expressions, finite symbol strings, and finite graphs of arbitrary size are also countable; this follows by finite-string encoding, not from a survey of existing examples.

FormalExpression.scope: Algorithm, Computable function, and Recursive function — each countably infinite under the usual finite-description convention. Finite formal expressions, finite symbol strings, and finite graphs of arbitrary size are also countable; this follows by finite-string encoding, not from a survey of existing examples.
FormalExpression.interpretation: Finite symbolic descriptions over a fixed countable encoding; not arbitrary infinite strings.

SymbolicString.scope: Algorithm, Computable function, and Recursive function — each countably infinite under the usual finite-description convention. Finite formal expressions, finite symbol strings, and finite graphs of arbitrary size are also countable; this follows by finite-string encoding, not from a survey of existing examples.
SymbolicString.interpretation: Finite symbolic descriptions over a fixed countable encoding; not arbitrary infinite strings.

Graph.scope: Algorithm, Computable function, and Recursive function — each countably infinite under the usual finite-description convention. Finite formal expressions, finite symbol strings, and finite graphs of arbitrary size are also countable; this follows by finite-string encoding, not from a survey of existing examples.
Graph.interpretation: Finite graphs up to isomorphism, or with vertices in a fixed countable encoding; not all infinitely large or arbitrarily labelled graphs.

Function.scope: Function — 2^ℵ₀ functions from natural numbers to natural numbers; no single cardinality applies without fixing the domain and codomain. Set likewise has no universal set of all sets in ordinary set theory, so it receives no total.
